Priyom / Steph — draft below for GlacierBank (feel free to edit). I also attached a simple timezone matrix and the proposed roster.

Proposed support + TAM coverage (summary):
- Go-live stabilization (first 90 days): dedicated TAM coverage with 8-hour overlap window between customer SRE shift and Redwood TAM for each critical region. Overlap windows we recommend:
  - US (ET) customer SRE shift 08:00–16:00 ET -> Redwood TAM overlap 12:00–20:00 ET (4-hour guaranteed overlap + on-call escalation).
  - EU (CET) customer SRE shift 09:00–17:00 CET -> Redwood TAM overlap 11:00–19:00 CET.
- Post-stabilization: TAM provides regional office hours (09:00–18:00 local) with 24/7 on-call rotation for severity >= P1 escalations.

Acknowledgement and communication cadence (incident class P1):
- Acknowledgement SLA: 15 minutes (TAM or on-call engineer confirms ticket and initial owner).
- Initial customer-facing update: within 60 minutes with current impact, mitigation steps in progress, owner, and next update ETA.
- Follow-up cadence: hourly updates until service is triaged to mitigation, then cadence agreed with customer (e.g., every 4 hours).

Escalation path (ordered):
1) Assigned TAM (primary) — first point for customer comms and coordination.
2) TAM Lead — for coverage gaps or if TAM is unreachable within SLA window.
3) Support Engineering on-call (pager) — for technical triage and hot fixes.
4) Regional SRE (Redwood) — for infra-level remediation and cross-region failover.
5) Executive escalation (Sales + Customer Success) — in incidents impacting SLA or contractual uptime.

Operational notes:
- Handoffs will use an agreed Slack channel with a pinned incident thread + a weekly cross-team sync during the 90-day window.
- All P1/P0 incidents produce a post-incident report within 72 hours for joint review.

See attached: GlacierBank-TAM_Roster.xlsx and Incident-Notification-Templates.docx (templates include acknowledgement, status update, and post-incident summary).

-Neha
Neha Kapoor
